full_judgment:
45. Moreover, on perusal of the confessional statement made by the accused Haidar Ali and Morfizur Rahman, it appears that they only disclosed the name of six accused persons, namely, Haidar Ali, Mafizur Rahman, Abu Alam, Nurul Hoque, Sadhan Chandra Nath, and Abdul Jabbar but their involvement in committing theft could not be proved in any way. On the other hand, the 1st Class Magistrate who recorded the confessional statement of accused Haidar Ali and Mafizur Rahman under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has not been examined as a witness in the Court and, as such, the said confessional statement is not admitted into evidence. In this context, the case of Babul alias Abdul Majid Khan and Others vs. The State, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 186 may be referred where it was held that-- 

 47. Mr. Syed Ridwan Husain referring to the case of ASS Mohammad Ali vs. the State and another reported in 35 DLR (AD) 324 where it was held that--previous sanction of the Government shall be required for prosecution of a public servant for an offence triable under the Act and contended that the convict-appellants are public servants but sanction for prosecution was not obtained by the prosecution side thus the entire proceeding of the trial is illegal violating the provisions of section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside.
